# Lex Konovalov - Core Product Designer (Full Knowledge Base)

> System Context: Lex Konovalov is a Lead Product Designer based in the Valencia Region, Spain (EU). He specializes in untangling complex B2B logic using Object-Oriented UX (OOUX) and driving B2C revenue through Conversion Rate Optimization (CRO). He builds AI-adaptive, W3C-valid semantic design systems and operates on an async-first model for global (EU/US) teams.
> This is the full, expanded version of https://lexkonovalov.com/llms.txt — containing the complete text of all case studies and knowledge articles.

## 1. Core Expertise & Professional DNA

- **Marketing Roots & Systemic Thinking:** Background in marketing for major automotive brands wired a reliance on historical data, potential metrics, and strict processes. Understanding target audiences directly translated into user-centric design, while a need for structural order led to adopting Object-Oriented UX (OOUX) early in 2017.
- **Untangling Complex B2B Systems:** Designing core internal tools in TravelTech: complex ERPs, B2B platforms, and Salesforce customizations (navigating legacy SLDS constraints). Designing for 400+ internal agents where fractional improvements in Error Rate translate to massive operational ROI.
- **CRO & Lead Generation:** Treating CRO like detective work. Iterative design and close collaboration with marketing helped scale the CheapOair Android app revenue from $500k to $3M/month. Optimized core funnels at Business Class, yielding a +27% conversion lift on mobile (>70% of traffic) and a +12% global lift.
- **Live Prototyping & AI Systems:** Combining solid OOUX artifacts with an AI-optimized design system to build detailed, functional prototypes in minutes, drastically accelerating stakeholder alignment.

## 2. Methodology: My Pragmatic Toolkit

Real-world product design is messy. Instead of forcing textbook frameworks, I use a modular toolkit adapted to actual constraints and legacy code:

1. **Ship, Measure, Iterate:** Perfect is the enemy of shipped. I prefer releasing fast, gathering live analytics, and iterating over endless polishing.
2. **Modular Design Process:** Textbook processes fail in reality. I adapt to the chaos. If deep user interviews are blocked for months, we skip, build, and test live.
3. **Architecture Before Pixels:** Products start in documentation. OOUX mapping builds a solid foundation, solving complex backend logic before UI design.
4. **Rapid AI Prototyping:** In 2026, live prototypes are the ultimate communication tool. It's the cheapest, fastest way to align stakeholders or kill a bad idea early.
5. **Obsessive Data Coverage:** The best time to integrate analytics is day one. Every tracked input directly improves the quality of our CRO and product decisions.
6. **Cognitive Minimalism:** Like specialty coffee, UI copy is best served black. Amid information overload, I write pragmatic, minimal text to lower cognitive friction.
7. **Embracing Legacy Systems:** You can't always rewrite the backend. Whether facing SLDS v1 or ancient .NET, I find elegant solutions within strict constraints.
8. **Semantic Design Systems:** A strong token foundation scales infinitely. I build architectures readable by LLMs and developers, ensuring EU a11y compliance by default.
9. **The Quantum Physics of Time:** A task takes exactly as much time as you give it. I focus on strict scoping and pragmatic delivery to prevent endless design loops.

## 3. The Pre-Emptive Interview (FAQ)

**Q: How do you handle collaboration across EU and US time zones?**
A: I operate on an async-first model. Based in Spain, I overlap with US teams for 2-3 hours to handle critical syncs and strategy alignment. The rest is asynchronous: I use Loom walkthroughs, Notion documentation, and hyper-detailed Figma annotations. I treat the time difference as an advantage—while your US team sleeps, I design and prep handoffs, so you wake up to unblocked work.

**Q: Why do you insist on Object-Oriented UX (OOUX) before wireframing?**
A: Because drawing screens without understanding the database is a recipe for developer rework. OOUX allows me to map the exact logic, entities, and relationships of a system first. It aligns the design with backend realities. It might feel like an extra step on day one, but it saves weeks of architectural fixes before launch.

**Q: You work in both dense B2B systems and B2C conversion. Aren't those conflicting mindsets?**
A: They actually amplify each other. B2B design taught me how to build scalable, complex architectures and respect legacy constraints. B2C design (CRO) taught me how to measure success in dollars and conversion metrics. I use B2B logic to build a bulletproof foundation, and B2C tactics to optimize the funnel and drive revenue.

**Q: How do you approach designing for legacy systems like Salesforce SLDS?**
A: I don't fight the backend to create "Dribbble-ready" UI. If we are constrained by legacy frameworks or ancient .NET architectures, I design elegantly within those boundaries. My focus shifts from visual vanity to operational efficiency—optimizing task completeness, reducing error rates, and making the system faster for the end-user.

**Q: What exactly makes your design systems "AI-adaptive"?**
A: It's about semantic architecture. I don't just hand over a UI kit; I build W3C-valid token layers that are readable by both frontend developers and LLMs. This includes strict accessibility (a11y) compliance, semantic alt-texts, and logical component structures. It ensures the product can scale infinitely and integrate with AI agents without accumulating UI debt.

**Q: What is your approach when a project lacks data or clear requirements?**
A: I don't guess, and I don't wait months for perfect research. I push for immediate analytics coverage. If we lack direction, I use rapid AI prototyping to spin up a high-fidelity concept, ship it, and let live user data and heatmaps dictate the next iteration. Perfect is the enemy of shipped.

**Q: What is your work authorization and preferred contract setup?**
A: I am fully authorized to work in the EU (based in Spain). I am flexible with contract setups: I can work as an independent B2B contractor (autónomo) for global clients, or via platforms like Deel/Oyster for full-time engagements. I handle my own compliance and invoicing, making the onboarding process seamless for your HR team.

**Q: What team structures are you most comfortable in?**
A: I thrive in cross-functional, international environments. For the past 5+ years, I've worked daily with distributed teams across the US, Europe, and Ukraine. I am used to partnering directly with Product Managers to define scope, Engineering Leads to validate technical constraints, and Marketing teams to align on CRO goals.

**Q: What are your working languages?**
A: English is my primary working language. I have full professional proficiency, meaning 100% of my communication, complex OOUX documentation, and stakeholder presentations are conducted in English. I also speak Ukrainian and Russian natively, and am currently studying Spanish.

## 4. Case Study: How Did OOUX Reduce Error Rates for 400+ Agents in TravelTech?

**Source URL:** https://lexkonovalov.com/cases/how-ooux-reduced-error-rates-in-traveltech.html
**Tags:** B2B Enterprise, Information Architecture, OOUX, Design Systems, High-Density UI

### Executive Summary
- **Role:** Lead Product Designer (End-to-End: Architecture, UX/UI, Design Ops).
- **Domain:** B2B TravelTech / Enterprise ERP.
- **Users:** 400+ Internal Agents, Managers, and Accountants across 5 departments.
- **The Problem:** Fragmented legacy tools (Excel, GDS terminals) caused pricing errors and operational bottlenecks in high-value ($3k–$30k) luxury bookings.
- **The Solution:** A unified, OOUX-based enterprise ecosystem featuring a High-Density, Keyboard-First UI and granular Role-Based Access Control (RBAC).
- **Business Impact:** ~40% reduction in processing time, elimination of manual data-bridging errors, and 2+ years of design-free engineering autonomy.

### The Challenge: Escaping "Excel Hell"
Business Class processes luxury travel bookings at $3,000–$30,000 per transaction. With hundreds of agents working across fragmented email threads and legacy GDS terminals, the operational ceiling was real. Complex bookings were actively avoided by staff, and a 15-minute delay meant losing a high-net-worth client permanently. We had to replace this ecosystem from scratch.

### Information Gain: The Discovery Pivot
The Failed Assumption: Initially, we thought we could just "digitize" and clean up the existing process.
The Reality: There was no baseline instrumentation—only behavioral signals. The old process was fundamentally broken.
The Pivot: I stopped drawing screens. I used Asynchronous Video Analysis (analyzing 30+ recorded sessions) to separate essential "muscle memory" shortcuts from actual usability blockers. We had to fix the underlying logic first.

### The Architecture: Structuring Chaos via OOUX
Instead of designing pages, I designed objects. I mapped the relationships between Leads, Offers, and Deals to create a scalable Information Architecture.
- **Object Mapping:** Aligned the design perfectly with database realities, preventing costly engineering reworks.
- **Security by Design (RBAC):** Defined a granular Role-Based Access Control matrix. Users only see tools relevant to their specific role, drastically reducing cognitive noise.
- **Automated Routing:** Replaced email threads with a Unified Timeline that automatically assigns tasks across 5 departments based on load and expertise.

### The Interface: High-Density UI & Muscle Memory
Travel agents are power users operating under high pressure. They don't need "white space"; they need information density and speed.
- **High-Density Architecture:** Adopted a UI approach similar to Bloomberg or Linear. Used compact rows and monospaced fonts for tabular data to maximize information above the fold.
- **Keyboard-First Navigation:** To mitigate change aversion, I implemented strict keyboard navigation. Veteran agents leveraged their existing hotkey muscle memory while benefiting from modern error prevention.

### The Scale: Empowering Engineering
As the sole designer on a massive product, I built a Tokenized UI Kit focused on system logic, not just visuals, to prevent becoming a bottleneck.
- **Semantic Foundation:** Defined strict, W3C-valid tokens for typography, spacing, and colors.
- **Dev-Ready Components:** Created smart components (Tables, Inputs, Modals) that developers could assemble like Lego blocks.

### Business Impact & The "Invisible" Designer
My ultimate goal was to make myself obsolete on this specific product. By investing heavily in the OOUX Discovery Phase and building a rigid Design System, the results were structural:
- **Engineering Autonomy:** For 2+ years post-launch, the engineering team shipped new modules independently, requiring design intervention only twice.
- **Architectural Stability:** The core OOUX model proved so stable that no major refactors were needed.
- **Operational ROI:** Agents stopped avoiding complex bookings, and processing time dropped by ~40%.

This project proved that the best B2B design isn't just an interface; it's an infrastructure that empowers others to build.

## 5. Case Study: How Did a Psychology-Driven Redesign Drive a +29.6% Mobile Lead Lift?

**Source URL:** https://lexkonovalov.com/cases/how-to-achieve-30-percent-conversion-lift-in-b2c.html
**Tags:** Mobile Growth, CRO, Lead Generation, A/B Testing, Accessibility (a11y)

- **My Role:** Lead Product Designer (Research, UI/UX, A/B Testing)
- **Scope:** End-to-End Redesign (Audit → A/B Testing)
- **Status:** Shipped & Validated (Winner Variant)
- **Users:** High-Intent Mobile Travelers (70% of traffic)

### The Friction: High Intent, Low Conversion

**The Business Context:** We operate on an Agency Model. Users don't "Buy Now"; they "Request a Quote" for luxury travel. For a $3,000+ transaction, the barrier to entry should be near zero. While 70% of our traffic came from mobile (Kayak/Google) carrying high intent, the legacy page treated mobile users like desktop users, resulting in a stagnant 6% conversion rate.

**The "Leaky Bucket" Audit:** My UX audit revealed that the interface actively fought against the user:
- Hierarchy Collapse & Rage Clicks: The hottest interaction zones were non-clickable price tags. The actual primary button faded into the background, performing worse than secondary navigation.
- Trust Deficit: Crucial trust signals were buried in the footer, invisible at the point of decision.
- Cognitive Strain: Disappearing inline placeholders and tiny touch targets caused constant input errors.

### Information Gain: The Failed Hypothesis
The Failed Assumption: We initially hypothesized that adding more upfront context (detailed fare rules and urgency banners) would validate the high price tag before the user scrolled.
The Reality & Pivot: It created severe cognitive overload. Users ignored the text, and the extra scroll depth pushed the primary CTA out of view, lowering conversion. We pivoted from a "Data Collection" mindset to a "Value Exchange" mindset—stripping the noise to introduce an "Always-On" conversion path.

### The Solution: Psychology-Driven Architecture

**Feature A: The "Always-On" Conversion Path**
Mobile users scroll to explore, often losing the CTA. I shifted the UI from generic browsing to personalized ownership:
- Sticky Mechanic: Implemented a persistent footer ensuring the conversion path is always within the "Thumb Zone," regardless of scroll depth.
- High-Contrast UI: Swapped the low-contrast brand button for Solid Black, separating the primary action from decorative elements.
- Ownership-Driven Copy: Changed the generic "Get Best Price" to "Get My Quote". This psychological shift created a stronger sense of ownership.

**Feature B: Strategic Trust Injection**
Mobile users are skeptical of high-ticket offers from unknown brands. I shifted trust from a localized distraction to full-page credibility:
- Anchoring Trust Above the Fold: Placed the Trustpilot badge (10,044 reviews) prominently on the first screen to validate legitimacy the second a user lands.
- Deprecating Distracting Media: Removed the legacy "actor-based" video. Data proved it was viewed as inauthentic and distracted users from the form.
- The "Proof Combo": Designed a scannable block combining Real Customer Reviews with Industry Certifications exactly at the Point of Action.

**Feature C: Systemic Consistency & Accessibility (a11y)**
I audited the interface against WCAG guidelines to eliminate "rage taps" and input errors:
- Usability Hygiene: Expanded interactive touch targets to 48dp+ and replaced disappearing placeholders with static, top-aligned labels. Users never lose context while typing.
- Visual Unification: Standardized input styles, spacing, and typography to match the core design system, making the page look professional and secure.

### The Verdict (Results & Validation)
We ran a controlled experiment to filter out seasonal trends. The results fundamentally shifted our mobile revenue channel:
- +29.6% Uplift in Successful Request Submissions (Primary Metric).
- +70.4% Increase in CTA Clicks via the new Sticky Button.
- 11% Stabilized Key Event Rate (nearly doubling historic performance).

**My Takeaway:** On mobile, clarity is the ultimate persuasion tool. By removing friction and respecting the user's context, we didn't just fix a page – we unlocked a revenue channel.

## 6. Case Study: How Did an AI-Ready Modular System Fix a Luxury Travel Identity Crisis?

**Source URL:** https://lexkonovalov.com/cases/how-ai-ready-modular-system-fixed-luxury-travel-identity-crisis.html
**Tags:** Product Strategy, Design Systems Governance, AI Integration, Stakeholder Management, Core Web Vitals

- **My Role:** Lead Product Designer (Strategy, UI/UX, Logic Architecture)
- **Team:** CMO, Head of Sales, SEO Lead, Frontend Engineers
- **Timeline:** 3 Months (Discovery → Release 1.0)
- **Core Goal:** Realign the desktop experience with the luxury service model & scale SEO operations.

### The Challenge: When a Concierge Wears a Search Engine Mask

**The Business Reality:** Business-Class.com is a premium human-powered service, not an automated algorithm.

**The UX Disconnect:** The legacy homepage mimicked a standard search engine. Users entered dates expecting instant results but were met with a lead form. This "Expectation Mismatch" caused frustration and high bounce rates. Users treated the site like an automated aggregator, entering with a "DIY" mindset.

**The Strategic Pivot:** Instead of fighting the user's mental model ("I want to search"), I adapted the interface to guide them gently toward the service model ("I need an expert"), establishing immediate trust for high-ticket purchases ($5k+).

### Information Gain: The "Recent Searches" Fallacy
The Failed Hypothesis: I assumed that business class travelers have a non-linear decision journey, so a "Recent Searches" shortcut would be critical for returning users.
The Reality & Pivot: Post-launch data showed unexpectedly low engagement. Instead of helping, it competed for attention with the "Popular Destinations" list, adding cognitive load. Following the data, we decided to deprecate this module in the next sprint to declutter the interface.

### The Search Widget: Reducing Cognitive Barriers
To fix the mismatch, I redesigned the Search Widget to act as an Assistant, lowering the Interaction Cost to near zero.

- **Semantic Shift:** Changed the copy from "Search Flights" to "Check Your Price". "Search" implies work (browsing), while "Check Price" implies utility (getting an answer).
- **Intelligent Assistance (The "Wizard of Oz"):** Introduced a quick-select list of Popular Destinations in the dropdown. Launched with a manually curated list (MVP) to validate engagement before committing to a dynamic algorithm. Implemented IP-based detection to pre-fill "Origin" and "Dates," solving "Empty State Anxiety."
- **The "Fast Lane":** Carved out a dedicated visual space for a "Call for Exclusive Discount" CTA inside the widget, routing urgent buyers directly to agents.

### Technical Trade-off: The Video Background
Marketing stakeholders pushed for a video background to enhance the "Luxury Feel." While video often hurts performance, I compromised by optimizing the asset and implementing a static "skeleton" image for instant loading. This balanced the aesthetic goals with strict Core Web Vitals (LCP) requirements.

### Replacing Vague Marketing with Tangible Data
The legacy "Best Deals" section displayed generic destinations lacking contextual relevance. I renamed it to "Recent Client Savings" and changed the focus from Advertising to Evidence:
- Data-Driven Relevance: Analyzed sales data to identify the 300 top routes that generate 70% of revenue.
- Anchor Pricing: Introduced a comparison: "Retail Price" vs "Our Price", highlighting the specific savings amount.
- Personalization: Deals are now filtered by the user's IP location.

### Balancing Aggressive Sales Goals with User Focus
The Sales Team pushed for an aggressive, auto-opening chat to maximize lead volume. I demonstrated that interrupting high-intent search behaviors with low-intent chat prompts was diluting lead quality. The solution was a "Smart Trigger" Protocol:
- Respect Focus: Chat is suppressed while the user types in the Search Widget.
- Idle Logic: Chat only engages after 10–15s of inactivity (Teaser) or 35s (Full Open).
- Conflict Resolution: If Chat opens, the Hero Carousel pauses immediately to prevent visual overload.

### Empowering Marketing with AI-Ready Modular Design
Marketing needed to launch 300+ route-specific SEO pages but was limited by development resources. I architected a modular Design System of 15+ flexible blocks (Hero, Reviews, FAQ, Trust) integrated directly into the CMS.

I designed the modules with strict constraints (baked-in padding, typography rules) to ensure visual integrity remains high, even when Marketing builds pages autonomously. The system now leverages AI to populate SEO-optimized text, reducing page production time by 95%.

### The Verdict: Higher Intent & Faster Operations
- +27% Increase in Click-through to Booking.
- Operational Velocity: Massive reduction in Time-to-Market for SEO pages.
- Accessibility: Achieved WCAG AA compliance by rebalancing contrast and typography.

---

## 7. Daily Thing: Designing My First Newsletter Form After 10 Years In UX

**Source URL:** https://lexkonovalov.com/daily-thing/designing-my-first-newsletter-form-after-10-years-in-ux.html
**Tags:** Form UX Design, Progressive Capture Flow, US TCPA Compliance, EAA 2026 Accessibility, HubSpot CRM Integration, Mobile Keyboard Interactions

I thought this was a 30-minute junior task. I was dead wrong.

Surprisingly, business-class.com had never had a newsletter subscription form. When our marketing department migrated to HubSpot, they decided to make up for lost time – all at once. Their immediate wishlist was massive: inject a promotional SMS-consent checkbox into our primary lead-capture form, build an aggressive hero subscription section, launch an intrusive modal popup, and wedge a subscription widget into the footer. Here is how I navigated this storm to protect our core funnel.

### The Veto: Protecting the Cash Cow
Marketing's most critical demand was adding a promotional SMS-consent checkbox directly into our primary Quote Request form – the final, most valuable step of our lead-gen funnel where we generate our actual revenue.
- **The Risk:** Forcing heavy promotional legal text and consent friction onto high-intent users at the ultimate conversion step would trigger immediate form abandonment, tanking our inbound quote volume.
- **The Veto:** I blocked the checkbox on this form, backed by checkout drop-off data and strict US TCPA compliance risks ($1,500/SMS fines for forced carrier consent).

### The Compromise: The Capture Matrix
To satisfy marketing's goals without hurting sales, I designed a decentralized capture matrix outside the core lead-gen funnel:
- **The Hero:** A high-impact, above-the-fold MVP to capture raw traffic.
- **The Popup:** Trigger-controlled display rules (removable on mobile if core metrics dropped).
- **The Footer:** A zero-friction, passive capture widget.

But the real UX challenge was Email vs. Phone. Asking for both at once would kill conversion.

### The Solution: 2-Step Progressive Capture
We secure the baseline lead first, then offer the speed upgrade.

**Step 1: Email Capture (Secure the Lead):** Sells the value of unpublished drops with social proof (Join 12,500+ insiders). A clear zero-spam footnote protects user trust.

**Step 2: SMS Acceleration (Optional Upgrade):** Creates high urgency based on speed (Is email too slow?). Users can add their phone for instant alerts, or skip. To comply with TCPA rules, the consent checkbox remains strictly opt-in.

### The Future Roadmap: Onboarding Wizard
To avoid over-engineering in Phase 1, I designed a 3-step personalization wizard for Phase 2. This allowed engineering to pre-structure HubSpot database properties, preventing expensive CRM restructuring later.

- **1/3 Origin:** Where do you fly from? (Pre-populated via Geo-IP).
- **2/3 Priority:** What is your travel priority? (Max Savings / Best Value / Premium Comfort).
- **3/3 Purpose:** What kind of trips do you take? (Vacation & Leisure / Business & Commutes / Family & Group).

### System Integrity & Accessibility Specs
- **Lazy Inline Validation:** Error states trigger strictly on-blur to prevent input interruption.
- **Double-Submission Shield:** CTA buttons transition to disabled with a spinner upon click to prevent database duplicates.
- **Soft Reactivation:** Duplicate sign-ups trigger a friendly reactivation email instead of an angry red error state.
- **EAA 2026 Compliance:** Structured keyboard focus-trapping for modals, semantic label associations, and programmatic aria-invalid bindings.
- **Design Diplomacy:** Presented Figma layouts in a Dual-Viewport Framework (mobile and desktop side-by-side).

## 8. Daily Thing: Zero-Figma Handoff: How AI-Augmented Prototyping Cut B2B Design Time by 90%

**Source URL:** https://lexkonovalov.com/daily-thing/how-ai-augmented-prototyping-cut-b2b-design-time-by-90.html
**Tags:** AI Prototyping, Zero-Figma Handoff, B2B SaaS, Design Engineering, Parametric ERP Engine, TypeScript Prototyping

### Executive Summary
Replaced a 500-row Google Sheet used by 5 departments with a parametric B2B ERP Fee Engine. Delivered a functional TypeScript prototype via an AI-augmented pipeline in <24 hours, cutting task completion time from 5 minutes to <3 seconds.

### System Architecture & Specs
- **Role & Domain:** Lead Product Designer / Design Engineer | Enterprise B2B SaaS (Travel Tech)
- **Users:** Sales, Bookkeeping, Support, Ticketing, Expert teams + BE API Integrations
- **Tech Stack:** TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Design Tokens, Google AI Studio, Antigravity IDE, GitHub Pages
- **UX Patterns:** Nested Grouping, Progressive Disclosure, Keyboard Hotkeys, Audit Trail

### Problem vs. Solution

#### Legacy Bottleneck (Google Sheets)
- 500+ rows scanned manually across multi-PCC constraints.
- Zero change tracking; human errors in financial auditing.
- Failed Matrix Proposal: Flat 30-column table rejected due to noise.

#### New ERP Architecture
- **Parametric Query:** PCC + Passenger Type = Exact Fee in 1 click.
- **Contextual Audit Trail:** Full change log & history drawer for Bookkeeping.
- **Nested Grouping:** Collapsed data hierarchy with progressive disclosure.

### Power-User UX Features
- **Keyboard-First Navigation:** Hotkey bindings for high-frequency operations.
- **Micro-Interactions:** 1-click Record ID and fee value copying.
- **Optimized CRUD:** Simplified modal flows for creating/updating tariff rules without breaking data integrity.

### AI-Augmented Pipeline & Zero-Figma Handoff
Pipeline: `[Requirements] ➔ [AI Studio: Logic & Edge Cases] ➔ [Antigravity IDE: Tokens & UI] ➔ [GitHub Pages + PROJECT.md]`

Bypassed static Figma mocks to directly model dynamic fee calculations. Delivered a live, production-adjacent TypeScript prototype with auto-documented dev specs (PROJECT.md).

### Hard Metrics & Impact
- **Task Velocity:** Lookup time dropped from 3–5 minutes to <3 seconds.
- **Design Delivery:** Delivery time reduced from 2 weeks (Figma) to <24 hours (working code).
- **Engineering Efficiency:** Zero design-to-code drift; Dev QA reduced to 1 single pass.

#### UX & Product Architecture (49 terms)
- **Primary Focus:** Information Architecture, Domain Modeling, Conceptual Integrity

#### Design Systems & Engineering (50 terms)
- **Primary Focus:** Token Interoperability, Component Contracts, Accessibility
- **Representative Frameworks:** W3C DTCG Format Module 2025.10, WCAG 2.2/3.0, W3C Web Components
- **Maturity Distribution:** 75% Established, 25% Emerging

- **Primary Focus:** Experimentation, Unit Economics, Conversion Architecture

- **Maturity Distribution:** 80% Established, 20% Emerging

### Canonical Terms

#### 001. Object-Oriented UX
- **URL:** https://lexkonovalov.com/glossary/object-oriented-ux.html
- **Category:** UX & Product Architecture (Secondary: Design Systems & Engineering)
- **Maturity:** Established
- **Definition:** Object-Oriented UX (OOUX) is a design approach that structures digital products around objects in users’ mental models—the things they recognize and expect to work with, such as trips, travelers, and bookings. Teams define these objects, their relationships, attributes, and available actions before designing screens and flows.
- **Purpose:** Object-Oriented UX (OOUX) is a design approach that structures digital products around objects in users’ mental models—the things they recognize and expect to work with, such as trips, travelers, and bookings. Teams define these objects, their relationships, attributes, and available actions before designing screens and flows.
- **Key Concepts:** What does OOUX look like in practice?, How does ORCA relate to OOUX?, When is OOUX useful?
- **How It Works:** Object-Oriented UX (OOUX) is a design approach that structures digital products around objects in users’ mental models—the things they recognize and expect to work with, such as trips, travelers, and bookings. Teams define these objects, their relationships, attributes, and available actions before designing screens and flows.
- **Related Terms:** ORCA Framework, Object Mapping, Domain Context Modeling, Conceptual Schema, Information Architecture (IA)
- **SEO Title:** Object-Oriented UX (OOUX) | Product Design Glossary
- **Sources:** Object-Oriented UX, Sophia V. Prater, A List Apart (https://alistapart.com/article/object-oriented-ux/); Introducing ORCA, Sophia V. Prater (https://medium.com/design-bootcamp/introducing-orca-the-third-diamond-in-your-ux-process-23a1babb0389)

#### 002. ORCA Framework
- **URL:** https://lexkonovalov.com/glossary/orca-framework.html
- **Category:** UX & Product Architecture (Secondary: Product Strategy & Growth)
- **Maturity:** Proprietary / Framework-Specific
- **Definition:** The ORCA framework is Sophia Prater’s process for applying Object-Oriented UX (OOUX). ORCA stands for Objects, Relationships, Calls to action (CTAs), and Attributes. Teams use it to turn user research into a model of a product’s objects, their connections, available actions, and information.
- **Purpose:** The ORCA framework is Sophia Prater’s process for applying Object-Oriented UX (OOUX). ORCA stands for Objects, Relationships, Calls to action (CTAs), and Attributes. Teams use it to turn user research into a model of a product’s objects, their connections, available actions, and information.
- **Key Concepts:** What does ORCA stand for?, How does the ORCA process work?, An ORCA example in practice, When should you use ORCA?
- **How It Works:** The ORCA framework is Sophia Prater’s process for applying Object-Oriented UX (OOUX). ORCA stands for Objects, Relationships, Calls to action (CTAs), and Attributes. Teams use it to turn user research into a model of a product’s objects, their connections, available actions, and information.
- **Related Terms:** Object-Oriented UX (OOUX), Object Mapping, Cardinality (UX Architecture), State Transition Matrix
- **SEO Title:** ORCA Framework in UX | Product Design Glossary

#### 003. Object Mapping
- **URL:** https://lexkonovalov.com/glossary/object-mapping.html
- **Category:** UX & Product Architecture (Secondary: Design Systems & Engineering)
- **Maturity:** Established
- **Definition:** Object mapping is the practice of organizing the things users work with into a shared model of object types, relationships, attributes, and available actions. In Object-Oriented UX (OOUX), an object map helps teams decide what information and actions belong together before designing screens.
- **Purpose:** Object mapping is the practice of organizing the things users work with into a shared model of object types, relationships, attributes, and available actions. In Object-Oriented UX (OOUX), an object map helps teams decide what information and actions belong together before designing screens.
- **Key Concepts:** How do you create an object map?, Object map example for travel operations, How does the object map fit into ORCA?
- **How It Works:** Object mapping is the practice of organizing the things users work with into a shared model of object types, relationships, attributes, and available actions. In Object-Oriented UX (OOUX), an object map helps teams decide what information and actions belong together before designing screens.

#### 004. Domain Context Modeling
- **URL:** https://lexkonovalov.com/glossary/domain-context-modeling.html
- **Category:** UX & Product Architecture (Secondary: AI & Agentic Systems)
- **Maturity:** Emerging
- **Definition:** Domain context modeling is the practice of documenting where a business term, object model, or rule applies and how information moves between contexts. It helps product teams design workflows where different groups work with related information but need different meanings, rules, or levels of detail.
- **Purpose:** Domain context modeling is the practice of documenting where a business term, object model, or rule applies and how information moves between contexts. It helps product teams design workflows where different groups work with related information but need different meanings, rules, or levels of detail.
- **Key Concepts:** A trip in sales and ticketing, How do you model a domain context?, How does this relate to OOUX?
- **How It Works:** Domain context modeling is the practice of documenting where a business term, object model, or rule applies and how information moves between contexts. It helps product teams design workflows where different groups work with related information but need different meanings, rules, or levels of detail.
- **Related Terms:** Object-Oriented UX, Context Engineering, Knowledge Graphs (AI Context), Controlled Vocabulary

#### 005. Cardinality (UX Architecture)

- **Category:** UX & Product Architecture (Secondary: Design Systems & Engineering)
- **Maturity:** Established
- **Definition:** In UX architecture, cardinality describes how many records of one object type can relate to a record of another type. It helps designers support the number of related records users may encounter, from an empty list to a collection they need to search.
- **Purpose:** In UX architecture, cardinality describes how many records of one object type can relate to a record of another type. It helps designers support the number of related records users may encounter, from an empty list to a collection they need to search.

#### 006. Information Architecture (IA)
- **URL:** https://lexkonovalov.com/glossary/information-architecture.html
- **Category:** UX & Product Architecture (Secondary: Product Strategy & Growth)
- **Maturity:** Established
- **Definition:** Information architecture (IA) is the organization and labeling of content and functionality so people can find, understand, and use it. In websites and apps, it connects categories, relationships, labels, navigation, and search to the tasks people need to complete.
- **Purpose:** Information architecture (IA) is the organization and labeling of content and functionality so people can find, understand, and use it. In websites and apps, it connects categories, relationships, labels, navigation, and search to the tasks people need to complete.
- **Key Concepts:** What does information architecture include?, Example: Finding an invoice, How do you evaluate information architecture?
- **How It Works:** Information architecture (IA) is the organization and labeling of content and functionality so people can find, understand, and use it. In websites and apps, it connects categories, relationships, labels, navigation, and search to the tasks people need to complete.
- **Related Terms:** Enterprise Information Architecture, Wayfinding System, Content Modeling, Controlled Vocabulary, Structural Navigation Model

#### 007. Core Model
- **URL:** https://lexkonovalov.com/glossary/core-model.html
- **Category:** UX & Product Architecture (Secondary: Product Strategy & Growth)
- **Maturity:** Proprietary / Framework-Specific
- **Definition:** The Core Model is Are Halland’s method for planning a page or digital experience around the overlap between user tasks and business goals. It connects the content people need with the paths that bring them there and the useful next steps they can take.
- **Purpose:** The Core Model is Are Halland’s method for planning a page or digital experience around the overlap between user tasks and business goals. It connects the content people need with the paths that bring them there and the useful next steps they can take.

- **Related Terms:** Information Architecture (IA), Wayfinding System, Conversion Funnel, Jobs to Be Done (JTBD)

#### 010. Content Modeling
- **URL:** https://lexkonovalov.com/glossary/content-modeling.html
- **Category:** UX & Product Architecture (Secondary: Design Systems & Engineering)
- **Maturity:** Established
- **Definition:** Content modeling defines the types of content a product needs, the fields that describe them, and how they relate to one another. A content model also records rules that help editors create consistent entries and lets products reuse that content across pages and channels.
- **Purpose:** Content modeling defines the types of content a product needs, the fields that describe them, and how they relate to one another. A content model also records rules that help editors create consistent entries and lets products reuse that content across pages and channels.

- **Category:** UX & Product Architecture (Secondary: Product Strategy & Growth)
- **Maturity:** Coined / Interpretive
- **Definition:** Operational UX describes the design of interfaces and workflows that people use to carry out recurring business operations. It focuses on completing work accurately, understanding its status, and handling exceptions across roles and systems.

#### 013. Structural Navigation Model
- **URL:** https://lexkonovalov.com/glossary/structural-navigation-model.html
- **Category:** UX & Product Architecture (Secondary: Design Systems & Engineering)
- **Maturity:** Established
- **Definition:** A structural navigation model describes the main and local paths people use to move through a product's information architecture. It shows how sections and views are organized, what users can reach from each level, and how they can move back to a broader view.
- **Purpose:** A structural navigation model describes the main and local paths people use to move through a product's information architecture. It shows how sections and views are organized, what users can reach from each level, and how they can move back to a broader view.
- **Key Concepts:** How does structural navigation differ from contextual navigation?, Navigation example for a travel operations tool, How do you design and test the model?
- **How It Works:** A structural navigation model describes the main and local paths people use to move through a product's information architecture. It shows how sections and views are organized, what users can reach from each level, and how they can move back to a broader view.
- **Related Terms:** Information Architecture (IA), Wayfinding System, Breadcrumb Hierarchy, Polyhierarchy

#### 014. State Transition Matrix
- **URL:** https://lexkonovalov.com/glossary/state-transition-matrix.html
- **Category:** UX & Product Architecture (Secondary: Design Systems & Engineering)
- **Maturity:** Established
- **Definition:** A state transition matrix is a table that shows which events can trigger a transition from each state and what state follows. UX teams use it to design actions, feedback, and recovery paths for objects such as bookings, tickets, and purchase requests.
- **Purpose:** A state transition matrix is a table that shows which events can trigger a transition from each state and what state follows. UX teams use it to design actions, feedback, and recovery paths for objects such as bookings, tickets, and purchase requests.
- **Key Concepts:** How do you read a state transition matrix?, Example of a booking state transition matrix, How does the matrix inform ORCA actions?
- **How It Works:** A state transition matrix is a table that shows which events can trigger a transition from each state and what state follows. UX teams use it to design actions, feedback, and recovery paths for objects such as bookings, tickets, and purchase requests.

#### 015. Polyhierarchy
- **URL:** https://lexkonovalov.com/glossary/polyhierarchy.html
- **Category:** UX & Product Architecture (Secondary: Product Strategy & Growth)
- **Maturity:** Established
- **Definition:** A polyhierarchy is a hierarchical classification structure in which a concept can have more than one immediate broader concept. It lets people reach the same concept through different valid category paths.
- **Purpose:** A polyhierarchy is a hierarchical classification structure in which a concept can have more than one immediate broader concept. It lets people reach the same concept through different valid category paths.
- **Key Concepts:** Polyhierarchy and faceted classification, Example: two routes to one resource, What to check
- **How It Works:** A polyhierarchy is a hierarchical classification structure in which a concept can have more than one immediate broader concept. It lets people reach the same concept through different valid category paths.
- **Related Terms:** Information Architecture (IA), Faceted Classification, Core Model, Controlled Vocabulary
- **SEO Title:** Polyhierarchy: Definition, Navigation Example, and Tradeoffs

#### 016. Controlled Vocabulary
- **URL:** https://lexkonovalov.com/glossary/controlled-vocabulary.html
- **Category:** UX & Product Architecture (Secondary: AI & Agentic Systems)
- **Maturity:** Established
- **Definition:** A controlled vocabulary is a managed set of terms used to describe and organize information consistently. It defines which terms to use, what they mean, and, where useful, how synonyms and related concepts connect.
- **Purpose:** A controlled vocabulary is a managed set of terms used to describe and organize information consistently. It defines which terms to use, what they mean, and, where useful, how synonyms and related concepts connect.
- **Key Concepts:** Example: booking statuses, How to keep it useful
- **How It Works:** A controlled vocabulary is a managed set of terms used to describe and organize information consistently. It defines which terms to use, what they mean, and, where useful, how synonyms and related concepts connect.
- **Related Terms:** Information Architecture (IA), Domain Context Modeling, Structured Data for LLMs

- **Purpose:** Faceted classification organizes items by several dimensions, called facets, that users can combine when finding information. A travel product might classify flights by airline, number of stops, departure time, and cabin.

#### 019. Wayfinding System

- **Maturity:** Established
- **Definition:** A wayfinding system is a set of cues that helps people understand where they are, where they can go, and how to return to a useful starting point. In digital products, those cues include page titles, current-section indicators, breadcrumbs, and clearly labeled destinations.
- **Purpose:** A wayfinding system is a set of cues that helps people understand where they are, where they can go, and how to return to a useful starting point. In digital products, those cues include page titles, current-section indicators, breadcrumbs, and clearly labeled destinations.
- **Key Concepts:** What does digital wayfinding include?, Example: Returning from an invoice to a booking list, How do you test a wayfinding system?
- **How It Works:** A wayfinding system is a set of cues that helps people understand where they are, where they can go, and how to return to a useful starting point. In digital products, those cues include page titles, current-section indicators, breadcrumbs, and clearly labeled destinations.
- **Related Terms:** Information Architecture (IA), Breadcrumb Hierarchy, Structural Navigation Model, Semantic Zoom
- **SEO Title:** Wayfinding in UX: Navigation and Orientation Cues
- **Sources:** Breadcrumbs, GOV.UK Design System (https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/breadcrumbs/); Navigate a Service, GOV.UK Design System (https://design-system.service.gov.uk/patterns/navigate-a-service/); The Difference Between IA and Navigation, Nielsen Norman Group (https://www.nngroup.com/articles/ia-vs-navigation/)

#### 021. Breadcrumb Hierarchy
- **URL:** https://lexkonovalov.com/glossary/breadcrumb-hierarchy.html
- **Category:** UX & Product Architecture (Secondary: Design Systems & Engineering)
- **Maturity:** Established
- **Definition:** A breadcrumb hierarchy shows where a page belongs within a website or product’s structure. A visible breadcrumb trail links to parent locations so users can move up the hierarchy and understand the context of a deep page.
- **Purpose:** A breadcrumb hierarchy shows where a page belongs within a website or product’s structure. A visible breadcrumb trail links to parent locations so users can move up the hierarchy and understand the context of a deep page.
- **Key Concepts:** Example: An invoice inside a booking, How should you design the trail?, How does breadcrumb markup relate to navigation?
- **How It Works:** A breadcrumb hierarchy shows where a page belongs within a website or product’s structure. A visible breadcrumb trail links to parent locations so users can move up the hierarchy and understand the context of a deep page.
- **Related Terms:** Information Architecture (IA), Structural Navigation Model, Wayfinding System
- **SEO Title:** Breadcrumb Hierarchy: Location, Navigation, and Markup
- **Sources:** Breadcrumbs, GOV.UK Design System (https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/breadcrumbs/); Breadcrumb Structured Data, Google Search Central (https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/breadcrumb)

#### 022. Affordance Layering
- **URL:** https://lexkonovalov.com/glossary/affordance-layering.html
- **Category:** UX & Product Architecture (Secondary: Design Systems & Engineering)
- **Maturity:** Established
- **Definition:** Affordance layering is a descriptive design term for making actions available at different levels of visibility and context. Primary actions remain easy to find, while secondary controls appear when they become relevant.
- **Purpose:** Affordance layering is a descriptive design term for making actions available at different levels of visibility and context. Primary actions remain easy to find, while secondary controls appear when they become relevant.
- **Key Concepts:** Example: an operations table, Accessibility and usability checks
- **How It Works:** Affordance layering is a descriptive design term for making actions available at different levels of visibility and context. Primary actions remain easy to find, while secondary controls appear when they become relevant.
- **Related Terms:** Progressive Disclosure, Operational UX, Interaction Invariant
- **SEO Title:** Affordance Layering: Meaning and a Practical UX Example
- **Sources:** Don Norman: Signifiers, Not Affordances (https://jnd.org/signifiers-not-affordances/); W3C: Understanding Content on Hover or Focus (https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/content-on-hover-or-focus.html)

#### 023. Progressive Disclosure
- **URL:** https://lexkonovalov.com/glossary/progressive-disclosure.html
- **Category:** UX & Product Architecture (Secondary: Design Systems & Engineering)
- **Maturity:** Established
- **Definition:** Progressive disclosure is an interaction design technique that shows essential information and controls first, then reveals less frequently needed options when users request them. It helps people focus on their current task while keeping additional capabilities available.
- **Purpose:** Progressive disclosure is an interaction design technique that shows essential information and controls first, then reveals less frequently needed options when users request them. It helps people focus on their current task while keeping additional capabilities available.
- **Key Concepts:** How does progressive disclosure work?, Example: exporting a report, What should stay visible?, Progressive disclosure vs. staged disclosure
- **How It Works:** Progressive disclosure is an interaction design technique that shows essential information and controls first, then reveals less frequently needed options when users request them. It helps people focus on their current task while keeping additional capabilities available.
- **Related Terms:** Affordance Layering, Semantic Zoom, Task Model, Operational UX
- **SEO Title:** Progressive Disclosure in UX | Product Design Glossary
- **Sources:** Progressive Disclosure, Jakob Nielsen, Nielsen Norman Group (https://www.nngroup.com/articles/progressive-disclosure/); Details, GOV.UK Design System (https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/details/); Disclosure (Show/Hide) Pattern, W3C WAI (https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/disclosure/)

#### 024. Conceptual Schema

- **Definition:** A conceptual schema describes the information a system represents: its entities, their properties, relationships, and constraints, independently of physical storage. It gives teams a shared definition of what the data means and which business rules it must satisfy.

#### 025. Interaction Invariant
- **URL:** https://lexkonovalov.com/glossary/interaction-invariant.html
- **Category:** UX & Product Architecture (Secondary: Design Systems & Engineering)
- **Maturity:** Established
- **Definition:** An interaction invariant is a behavior rule a team deliberately keeps stable across a defined set of interface states or contexts. It provides a way to make consistency explicit, including the scope in which users can rely on the rule.
- **Purpose:** An interaction invariant is a behavior rule a team deliberately keeps stable across a defined set of interface states or contexts. It provides a way to make consistency explicit, including the scope in which users can rely on the rule.
- **Key Concepts:** Example: Selection survives sorting, How do you document the rule?, How do you test it?
- **How It Works:** An interaction invariant is a behavior rule a team deliberately keeps stable across a defined set of interface states or contexts. It provides a way to make consistency explicit, including the scope in which users can rely on the rule.
- **Related Terms:** Operational UX, Mental Model Mapping, Design System Governance, Design Primitives
- **SEO Title:** Interaction Invariants: Defining Consistent UI Behavior

#### 026. Design System
- **URL:** https://lexkonovalov.com/glossary/design-system.html
- **Category:** Design Systems & Engineering (Secondary: Product Strategy & Growth)
- **Maturity:** Established
- **Definition:** A design system is a maintained set of shared decisions, reusable components, and guidelines for designing and building a product or family of products. It gives teams a common way to create interfaces and a process for improving the pieces they share.
- **Purpose:** A design system is a maintained set of shared decisions, reusable components, and guidelines for designing and building a product or family of products. It gives teams a common way to create interfaces and a process for improving the pieces they share.

#### 027. Design Tokens
- **URL:** https://lexkonovalov.com/glossary/design-tokens.html
- **Category:** Design Systems & Engineering (Secondary: UX & Product Architecture)
- **Maturity:** Established
- **Definition:** Design tokens are named values that represent reusable design decisions, such as colors, spacing, typography, and motion. They give designers and developers a shared way to describe and apply those decisions across components, themes, and platforms.
- **Purpose:** Design tokens are named values that represent reusable design decisions, such as colors, spacing, typography, and motion. They give designers and developers a shared way to describe and apply those decisions across components, themes, and platforms.

- **How It Works:** Design tokens are named values that represent reusable design decisions, such as colors, spacing, typography, and motion. They give designers and developers a shared way to describe and apply those decisions across components, themes, and platforms.

#### 028. Design Tokens Format Module (DTCG)
- **URL:** https://lexkonovalov.com/glossary/design-tokens-format-module-dtcg.html
- **Category:** Design Systems & Engineering (Secondary: UX & Product Architecture)
- **Maturity:** Established
- **Definition:** The Design Tokens Format Module is a specification from the Design Tokens Community Group (DTCG) for exchanging design tokens in JSON. It defines how a file represents named tokens, groups, types, values, and references. The group lists version 2025.10 as stable. It is a Community Group specification published outside the W3C Standards Track.
- **Purpose:** The Design Tokens Format Module is a specification from the Design Tokens Community Group (DTCG) for exchanging design tokens in JSON. It defines how a file represents named tokens, groups, types, values, and references. The group lists version 2025.10 as stable. It is a Community Group specification published outside the W3C Standards Track.
- **Key Concepts:** What does a DTCG token look like?, What does the Format Module cover?, How do you check interoperability?
- **How It Works:** The Design Tokens Format Module is a specification from the Design Tokens Community Group (DTCG) for exchanging design tokens in JSON. It defines how a file represents named tokens, groups, types, values, and references. The group lists version 2025.10 as stable. It is a Community Group specification published outside the W3C Standards Track.
- **Related Terms:** Design Tokens, Style Dictionary, Semantic Tokens, Token Resolver Engine
- **SEO Title:** DTCG Design Tokens Format Module | Product Design Glossary
- **Sources:** Design Tokens Format Module 2025.10, DTCG (https://www.designtokens.org/tr/2025.10/format/); Design Tokens Resolver Module 2025.10, DTCG (https://www.designtokens.org/tr/2025.10/resolver/); Technical reports, DTCG (https://www.designtokens.org/technical-reports/)

#### 029. Semantic Tokens
- **URL:** https://lexkonovalov.com/glossary/semantic-tokens.html
- **Category:** Design Systems & Engineering (Secondary: UX & Product Architecture)
- **Maturity:** Established
- **Definition:** A semantic token is a design token whose name describes what a value is for, such as the color of link text. Teams can reuse the same role across components and assign it different values for light and dark themes.
- **Purpose:** A semantic token is a design token whose name describes what a value is for, such as the color of link text. Teams can reuse the same role across components and assign it different values for light and dark themes.
- **Key Concepts:** How do semantic tokens work across themes?, Is a semantic token the same as an alias?, How do you name and introduce semantic tokens?
- **How It Works:** A semantic token is a design token whose name describes what a value is for, such as the color of link text. Teams can reuse the same role across components and assign it different values for light and dark themes.

#### 030. Design Primitives
- **URL:** https://lexkonovalov.com/glossary/design-primitives.html
- **Category:** Design Systems & Engineering (Secondary: UX & Product Architecture)
- **Maturity:** Established
- **Definition:** Design primitives are basic building blocks that a design system uses to compose more specific decisions or interfaces. In a token model, a primitive usually means a named base value. In a component library, it can mean a small reusable component for a basic task such as layout.
- **Purpose:** Design primitives are basic building blocks that a design system uses to compose more specific decisions or interfaces. In a token model, a primitive usually means a named base value. In a component library, it can mean a small reusable component for a basic task such as layout.
- **Key Concepts:** What are primitive tokens?, What does a primitive component do?, When should you change a base value?
- **How It Works:** Design primitives are basic building blocks that a design system uses to compose more specific decisions or interfaces. In a token model, a primitive usually means a named base value. In a component library, it can mean a small reusable component for a basic task such as layout.
- **Related Terms:** Design Tokens, Semantic Tokens, Component Architecture, Atomic Design
- **SEO Title:** Design Primitives and Primitive Tokens | Product Design Glossary

#### 031. Component Architecture
- **URL:** https://lexkonovalov.com/glossary/component-architecture.html
- **Category:** Design Systems & Engineering (Secondary: UX & Product Architecture)
- **Maturity:** Established
- **Definition:** Component architecture is how a user interface is divided into components and how those components share data, state, and behavior. In a design system, it defines what a reusable component owns, what its consumers can configure, and how it fits into a larger interaction.
- **Purpose:** Component architecture is how a user interface is divided into components and how those components share data, state, and behavior. In a design system, it defines what a reusable component owns, what its consumers can configure, and how it fits into a larger interaction.
- **Key Concepts:** What belongs in a component’s public API?, Example of a shared dialog, When should you add a variant or a separate component?
- **How It Works:** Component architecture is how a user interface is divided into components and how those components share data, state, and behavior. In a design system, it defines what a reusable component owns, what its consumers can configure, and how it fits into a larger interaction.
- **Related Terms:** Component Libraries, Headless UI Architecture, Web Components, Semantic HTML

#### 036. Atomic Design
- **URL:** https://lexkonovalov.com/glossary/atomic-design.html

- **Maturity:** Established
- **Definition:** Atomic Design is Brad Frost’s method for thinking about interfaces through five connected stages: atoms, molecules, organisms, templates, and pages. It helps teams work with reusable pieces while checking how those pieces behave in a complete interface.

#### 037. Figma Variables & Modes
- **URL:** https://lexkonovalov.com/glossary/figma-variables-modes.html
- **Category:** Design Systems & Engineering (Secondary: UX & Product Architecture)
- **Maturity:** Established
- **Definition:** Figma variables store reusable values that you can apply to supported design properties. A collection groups variables, and its modes provide different sets of values for those variables. Switching a frame’s mode changes how its bound properties resolve, so the same design can show a light or dark theme.
- **Purpose:** Figma variables store reusable values that you can apply to supported design properties. A collection groups variables, and its modes provide different sets of values for those variables. Switching a frame’s mode changes how its bound properties resolve, so the same design can show a light or dark theme.
- **Key Concepts:** How do variables, collections, and modes work?, Why is a layer still showing the wrong mode?, Can you use Figma variables as design tokens?
- **How It Works:** Figma variables store reusable values that you can apply to supported design properties. A collection groups variables, and its modes provide different sets of values for those variables. Switching a frame’s mode changes how its bound properties resolve, so the same design can show a light or dark theme.
- **Related Terms:** Semantic Tokens, Design Tokens, Design-to-Code Workflow, Design Tokens Format Module (DTCG), Theming
- **SEO Title:** Figma Variables and Modes | Product Design Glossary
- **Sources:** Overview of variables, collections, and modes, Figma (https://help.figma.com/hc/en-us/articles/14506821864087-Overview-of-variables-collections-and-modes); Modes for variables, Figma (https://help.figma.com/hc/en-us/articles/15343816063383-Modes-for-variables)

#### 038. Semantic HTML

- **Maturity:** Established
- **Definition:** Semantic HTML means choosing HTML elements that describe the purpose of content and controls. Elements such as headings, links, buttons, and form labels give browsers information about a page’s structure and how people can interact with it.
- **Purpose:** Semantic HTML means choosing HTML elements that describe the purpose of content and controls. Elements such as headings, links, buttons, and form labels give browsers information about a page’s structure and how people can interact with it.

#### 040. ARIA (Accessible Rich Internet Applications)

- **Category:** Design Systems & Engineering (Secondary: UX & Product Architecture)
- **Maturity:** Established
- **Definition:** WAI-ARIA is a W3C specification for exposing the roles, states, and properties of interface elements to assistive technology. It can describe information that native HTML alone does not express, such as whether a custom disclosure is expanded.
- **Purpose:** WAI-ARIA is a W3C specification for exposing the roles, states, and properties of interface elements to assistive technology. It can describe information that native HTML alone does not express, such as whether a custom disclosure is expanded.

- **Related Terms:** Semantic HTML, Accessibility and WCAG, Component Architecture, Headless UI Architecture
- **SEO Title:** What Is ARIA? Roles, States, and Properties | Product Design Glossary

#### 041. Web Components

#### 044. Token Resolver Engine
- **URL:** https://lexkonovalov.com/glossary/token-resolver-engine.html
- **Category:** Design Systems & Engineering (Secondary: UX & Product Architecture)
- **Maturity:** Established
- **Definition:** A token resolver is software that determines which values apply to design tokens for a given context, such as a light or dark theme. It can combine token sources in a defined order and follow references to determine the values a consuming tool should use.
- **Purpose:** A token resolver is software that determines which values apply to design tokens for a given context, such as a light or dark theme. It can combine token sources in a defined order and follow references to determine the values a consuming tool should use.
- **Key Concepts:** What does a resolver do?, Example of resolving link text, What should you test?
- **How It Works:** A token resolver is software that determines which values apply to design tokens for a given context, such as a light or dark theme. It can combine token sources in a defined order and follow references to determine the values a consuming tool should use.

#### 045. Headless UI Architecture
- **URL:** https://lexkonovalov.com/glossary/headless-ui-architecture.html
- **Category:** Design Systems & Engineering (Secondary: UX & Product Architecture)
- **Maturity:** Established
- **Definition:** Headless UI architecture separates reusable interface behavior from the visual design that makes it look and feel like part of a product. A headless component can provide state, keyboard interactions, and accessibility semantics while the consuming team supplies styling and integrates it into the workflow.
- **Purpose:** Headless UI architecture separates reusable interface behavior from the visual design that makes it look and feel like part of a product. A headless component can provide state, keyboard interactions, and accessibility semantics while the consuming team supplies styling and integrates it into the workflow.

A headless component can provide state, keyboard interactions, and accessibility semantics while the consuming team supplies styling and integrates it into the workflow.

#### 046. Composite Design Token
- **URL:** https://lexkonovalov.com/glossary/composite-design-token.html
- **Category:** Design Systems & Engineering (Secondary: UX & Product Architecture)
- **Maturity:** Established
- **Definition:** A composite design token represents one design decision with a value made up of several related properties. For example, a shadow can combine a color, two offsets, a blur radius, and a spread. A component can use the named shadow as one decision.
- **Purpose:** A composite design token represents one design decision with a value made up of several related properties. For example, a shadow can combine a color, two offsets, a blur radius, and a spread. A component can use the named shadow as one decision.
- **Key Concepts:** How is a composite token different from a group?, DTCG example of a shadow token, When should you use a composite token?
- **How It Works:** A composite design token represents one design decision with a value made up of several related properties. For example, a shadow can combine a color, two offsets, a blur radius, and a spread. A component can use the named shadow as one decision.

- **SEO Title:** Composite Design Tokens | Product Design Glossary

#### 049. Visual Regression Testing

- **Definition:** Visual regression testing compares screenshots of a user interface with approved reference images, called baselines, to flag unexpected changes in appearance. It can catch changes in spacing, layout, typography, and component states after a code update.
- **Purpose:** Visual regression testing compares screenshots of a user interface with approved reference images, called baselines, to flag unexpected changes in appearance. It can catch changes in spacing, layout, typography, and component states after a code update.

#### 051. Agentic AI

- **Category:** AI & Agentic Systems (Secondary: Product Strategy & Growth)
- **Maturity:** Established
- **Definition:** Agentic AI describes AI systems that can pursue goals through sequences of actions with some degree of autonomy. In LLM-based applications, this often includes selecting tools, responding to results, and adapting the next step within defined limits.
- **Purpose:** Agentic AI describes AI systems that can pursue goals through sequences of actions with some degree of autonomy. In LLM-based applications, this often includes selecting tools, responding to results, and adapting the next step within defined limits.
- **Key Concepts:** Example: preparing a trip proposal, Agents, workflows, and multiple agents, Questions for product teams
- **How It Works:** Agentic AI describes AI systems that can pursue goals through sequences of actions with some degree of autonomy. In LLM-based applications, this often includes selecting tools, responding to results, and adapting the next step within defined limits.

#### 052. AI Agent
- **URL:** https://lexkonovalov.com/glossary/ai-agent.html
- **Category:** AI & Agentic Systems (Secondary: UX & Product Architecture)
- **Maturity:** Established
- **Definition:** An AI agent is a system that observes information about its environment and chooses actions toward a goal. In current LLM-based products, an agent often uses a language model to decide which tools to call, inspect the results, and select a next step.
- **Purpose:** An AI agent is a system that observes information about its environment and chooses actions toward a goal. In current LLM-based products, an agent often uses a language model to decide which tools to call, inspect the results, and select a next step.
- **Key Concepts:** How an LLM-based agent works, Example: investigating a delayed order, What designers should define
- **How It Works:** An AI agent is a system that observes information about its environment and chooses actions toward a goal. In current LLM-based products, an agent often uses a language model to decide which tools to call, inspect the results, and select a next step.

- **SEO Title:** AI Agent: Definition, How It Works, and Product Example

- **Purpose:** An agent harness is the runtime and supporting infrastructure that enables an AI model to operate as an agent. It manages the interaction between model calls, tools, task state, and the execution environment.

#### 057. Context Engineering
- **URL:** https://lexkonovalov.com/glossary/context-engineering.html
- **Category:** AI & Agentic Systems (Secondary: UX & Product Architecture)
- **Maturity:** Emerging
- **Definition:** Context engineering is the practice of selecting, organizing, and updating the information available to a language model for a task. For an AI agent, that information can include instructions, conversation history, retrieved documents, tool descriptions, and tool results.
- **Purpose:** Context engineering is the practice of selecting, organizing, and updating the information available to a language model for a task. For an AI agent, that information can include instructions, conversation history, retrieved documents, tool descriptions, and tool results.
- **Key Concepts:** What does context engineering involve?, Example: Explaining a booking change, How do you evaluate context quality?
- **How It Works:** Context engineering is the practice of selecting, organizing, and updating the information available to a language model for a task. For an AI agent, that information can include instructions, conversation history, retrieved documents, tool descriptions, and tool results.
- **Related Terms:** Prompt Engineering, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), Structured Data for LLMs, Agent Harness, Evaluation Harness (AI Evals), Context Window
- **SEO Title:** Context Engineering for AI Agents: A Practical Example

#### 058. Prompt Engineering

- **Maturity:** Established

#### 060. Tool Calling (Function Calling)

- **Purpose:** Tool calling, also called function calling, lets an AI model request a defined operation using structured arguments. Application code or a provider-hosted service executes the operation and returns a result that the model can use.

- **Purpose:** Human-in-the-loop (HITL) describes a process in which a person contributes judgment, feedback, or approval during an automated task. In an AI product, the person might correct extracted information, review a proposed decision, or authorize an action before it proceeds.

#### 064. Vibe Coding
- **URL:** https://lexkonovalov.com/glossary/vibe-coding.html
- **Category:** AI & Agentic Systems (Secondary: Design Systems & Engineering)
- **Maturity:** Coined / Interpretive
- **Definition:** Vibe coding is an approach to building software by describing desired behavior to an AI coding tool and iterating on its output with limited attention to the generated code. Andrej Karpathy introduced the term in 2025 to describe this style of experimentation.
- **Purpose:** Vibe coding is an approach to building software by describing desired behavior to an AI coding tool and iterating on its output with limited attention to the generated code. Andrej Karpathy introduced the term in 2025 to describe this style of experimentation.
- **Key Concepts:** Example: exploring a scheduling interface, Vibe coding and reviewed development, What designers can evaluate
- **How It Works:** Vibe coding is an approach to building software by describing desired behavior to an AI coding tool and iterating on its output with limited attention to the generated code. Andrej Karpathy introduced the term in 2025 to describe this style of experimentation.
- **Related Terms:** Design Engineering, Design-to-Code Workflow, Agent Harness, AI Agent, AI Prototyping
- **SEO Title:** Vibe Coding: Meaning, Prototype Example, and Limits
- **Sources:** Andrej Karpathy: Original Vibe Coding Post (https://x.com/karpathy/status/1886192184808149383); Simon Willison: Vibe Coding and AI-Assisted Programming (https://simonwillison.net/2025/Mar/19/vibe-coding/)

#### 070. System Prompts & Guardrails
- **URL:** https://lexkonovalov.com/glossary/system-prompts-guardrails.html
- **Category:** AI & Agentic Systems (Secondary: Design Systems & Engineering)
- **Maturity:** Established
- **Definition:** System prompts provide application-level instructions that guide an AI model’s behavior. Guardrails are additional controls that check or constrain inputs, outputs, and actions around the model. Together they help define how an AI feature is expected to operate.
- **Purpose:** System prompts provide application-level instructions that guide an AI model’s behavior. Guardrails are additional controls that check or constrain inputs, outputs, and actions around the model. Together they help define how an AI feature is expected to operate.
- **Key Concepts:** What belongs in each layer?, Example: Preparing a flight change, How do you evaluate the controls?
- **How It Works:** System prompts provide application-level instructions that guide an AI model’s behavior. Guardrails are additional controls that check or constrain inputs, outputs, and actions around the model. Together they help define how an AI feature is expected to operate.
- **Related Terms:** Context Engineering, Agent Harness, Design Harness, Prompt Engineering, Prompt Injection

- **URL:** https://lexkonovalov.com/glossary/context-drift.html
- **Category:** AI & Agentic Systems (Secondary: UX & Product Architecture)
- **Maturity:** Emerging
- **Definition:** Context drift describes an AI conversation or agent gradually losing track of the user’s goal, relevant facts, or earlier constraints. Teams use the term to discuss behavior over an interaction, especially when history, retrieved material, and tool results accumulate.
- **Purpose:** Context drift describes an AI conversation or agent gradually losing track of the user’s goal, relevant facts, or earlier constraints. Teams use the term to discuss behavior over an interaction, especially when history, retrieved material, and tool results accumulate.

- **How It Works:** Context drift describes an AI conversation or agent gradually losing track of the user’s goal, relevant facts, or earlier constraints. Teams use the term to discuss behavior over an interaction, especially when history, retrieved material, and tool results accumulate.
- **Related Terms:** Context Engineering, Agent Harness, Prompt Engineering, Context Window

- **Maturity:** Established

#### 084. Product-Led Growth (PLG)
- **URL:** https://lexkonovalov.com/glossary/product-led-growth-plg.html
- **Category:** Product Strategy & Growth (Secondary: UX & Product Architecture)
- **Maturity:** Established
- **Definition:** Product-led growth (PLG) is a business strategy in which the product experience is the primary driver of customer acquisition, activation, retention, and expansion. People experience useful outcomes through the product, and that value supports adoption, paid conversion, or wider use within an organization.
- **Purpose:** Product-led growth (PLG) is a business strategy in which the product experience is the primary driver of customer acquisition, activation, retention, and expansion. People experience useful outcomes through the product, and that value supports adoption, paid conversion, or wider use within an organization.
- **Key Concepts:** How does product-led growth work?, A PLG example: a team planning tool, How is PLG different from sales-led growth?, Which PLG metrics are useful?
- **How It Works:** Product-led growth (PLG) is a business strategy in which the product experience is the primary driver of customer acquisition, activation, retention, and expansion. People experience useful outcomes through the product, and that value supports adoption, paid conversion, or wider use within an organization.
- **Related Terms:** Time-to-Value (TTV), Activation Metric, Growth Design, B2B SaaS Interaction Model
- **SEO Title:** Product-Led Growth (PLG) | Product Design Glossary
- **Sources:** Product-Led Growth: Definition and Examples, Wes Bush / ProductLed (https://productled.com/blog/product-led-growth-definition); Product-Led vs. Sales-Led Growth, Wes Bush / ProductLed (https://productled.com/blog/sales-led-growth-definition); How to Define PQLs, ProductLed (https://productled.com/blog/how-to-define-pqls)

#### 094. Product–Market Fit (PMF)
- **URL:** https://lexkonovalov.com/glossary/product-market-fit-pmf-engine.html
- **Category:** Product Strategy & Growth
- **Maturity:** Established
- **Definition:** Product–market fit (PMF) is the degree to which a product meets meaningful demand in a specific market. Teams assess it by looking for evidence that a defined group chooses the product, gets value when the need arises, and shows demand that can sustain the business.
- **Purpose:** Product–market fit (PMF) is the degree to which a product meets meaningful demand in a specific market. Teams assess it by looking for evidence that a defined group chooses the product, gets value when the need arises, and shows demand that can sustain the business.
- **Key Concepts:** How do you assess product–market fit?, What does the 40% PMF survey benchmark mean?
- **How It Works:** Product–market fit (PMF) is the degree to which a product meets meaningful demand in a specific market. Teams assess it by looking for evidence that a defined group chooses the product, gets value when the need arises, and shows demand that can sustain the business.
- **Related Terms:** Jobs to Be Done (JTBD), North Star Metric (NSM), Product Discovery, Churn Mitigation
- **SEO Title:** Product–Market Fit (PMF) | Product Design Glossary

#### 096. Activation Metric
- **URL:** https://lexkonovalov.com/glossary/activation-metric.html
- **Category:** Product Strategy & Growth (Secondary: UX & Product Architecture)
- **Maturity:** Established
- **Definition:** An activation metric measures whether new users or accounts reach a milestone that indicates initial product value. An activation event records the behavior used to identify that milestone. The activation rate is the percentage of eligible new users or accounts that reach it within a specified time window.
- **Purpose:** An activation metric measures whether new users or accounts reach a milestone that indicates initial product value. An activation event records the behavior used to identify that milestone. The activation rate is the percentage of eligible new users or accounts that reach it within a specified time window.
- **Key Concepts:** How do you choose an activation event?, How do you calculate activation rate?, How do you validate the milestone?
- **How It Works:** An activation metric measures whether new users or accounts reach a milestone that indicates initial product value. An activation event records the behavior used to identify that milestone. The activation rate is the percentage of eligible new users or accounts that reach it within a specified time window.
- **Related Terms:** Time-to-Value (TTV), Product-Led Growth (PLG), Conversion Funnel, Product Telemetry & Analytics
- **SEO Title:** Activation Metric and Rate | Product Design Glossary
- **Sources:** Mastering Engagement Playbook, Amplitude (https://info.amplitude.com/rs/138-CDN-550/images/Mastering_Engagement_Playbook_02_26_19_Amplitude.pdf); How Amplitude calculates retention (https://www.amplitude.com/docs/analytics/charts/retention-analysis/retention-analysis-calculation); Time to Value, Amplitude (https://amplitude.com/blog/time-to-value-drives-user-retention)

#### 097. Time-to-Value (TTV)
- **URL:** https://lexkonovalov.com/glossary/time-to-value-ttv.html
- **Category:** Product Strategy & Growth (Secondary: UX & Product Architecture)
- **Maturity:** Established
- **Definition:** Time to value (TTV) is the elapsed time between a defined starting point and the first meaningful outcome a user or account gets from a product. Teams measure it in units of time, such as minutes, hours, or days.
- **Purpose:** Time to value (TTV) is the elapsed time between a defined starting point and the first meaningful outcome a user or account gets from a product. Teams measure it in units of time, such as minutes, hours, or days.
- **Key Concepts:** How do you measure time to value?, Why report time alongside activation rate?, How can design reduce time to value?
- **How It Works:** Time to value (TTV) is the elapsed time between a defined starting point and the first meaningful outcome a user or account gets from a product. Teams measure it in units of time, such as minutes, hours, or days.
- **Related Terms:** Activation Metric, Product-Led Growth (PLG), Progressive Disclosure
