#### 102. Nested Object Matrix
- **URL:** https://lexkonovalov.com/glossary/nested-object-matrix.html
- **Category:** UX & Product Architecture (Secondary: Design Systems & Engineering)
- **Maturity:** Proprietary / Framework-Specific
- **Definition:** A Nested Object Matrix (NOM) is an ORCA grid that lists the same object types across its columns and down its rows. Each intersection describes how instances of one type relate to instances of the other. Teams use it to investigate relationships and identify where users may need access to related records.
- **Purpose:** A Nested Object Matrix (NOM) is an ORCA grid that lists the same object types across its columns and down its rows. Each intersection describes how instances of one type relate to instances of the other. Teams use it to investigate relationships and identify where users may need access to related records.
- **Key Concepts:** How do you read a Nested Object Matrix?, A Nested Object Matrix for travel operations, How do you build the matrix?
- **How It Works:** A Nested Object Matrix (NOM) is an ORCA grid that lists the same object types across its columns and down its rows. Each intersection describes how instances of one type relate to instances of the other. Teams use it to investigate relationships and identify where users may need access to related records.
- **Related Terms:** ORCA Framework, Object Mapping, Noun Foraging, Cardinality (UX Architecture)
- **SEO Title:** Nested Object Matrix in OOUX | Product Design Glossary
- **Sources:** Introducing ORCA, Sophia V. Prater (https://medium.com/design-bootcamp/introducing-orca-the-third-diamond-in-your-ux-process-23a1babb0389); Object-Oriented UX with Sophia Prater, InfoQ interview (https://www.infoq.com/podcasts/object-oriented-ux-sophia-prater/); Object-Oriented UX, Sophia V. #### 103. CTA Matrix
- **URL:** https://lexkonovalov.com/glossary/cta-matrix.html
- **Category:** UX & Product Architecture (Secondary: Design Systems & Engineering)
- **Maturity:** Proprietary / Framework-Specific
- **Definition:** A CTA Matrix, or call-to-action matrix, is an ORCA grid that maps user roles to object types and records the actions each role needs to take on each object. It gives teams a starting point for defining permissions, conditions, and interaction requirements before placing controls on screens.
- **Purpose:** A CTA Matrix, or call-to-action matrix, is an ORCA grid that maps user roles to object types and records the actions each role needs to take on each object. It gives teams a starting point for defining permissions, conditions, and interaction requirements before placing controls on screens.
- **Key Concepts:** What goes in a CTA Matrix?, CTA Matrix example for travel operations, How do you turn matrix entries into requirements?
- **How It Works:** A CTA Matrix, or call-to-action matrix, is an ORCA grid that maps user roles to object types and records the actions each role needs to take on each object. It gives teams a starting point for defining permissions, conditions, and interaction requirements before placing controls on screens.
- **Related Terms:** ORCA Framework, Object Mapping, Nested Object Matrix, State Transition Matrix
- **SEO Title:** CTA Matrix in OOUX | Product Design Glossary
- **Sources:** Introducing ORCA, Sophia V. Prater (https://medium.com/design-bootcamp/introducing-orca-the-third-diamond-in-your-ux-process-23a1babb0389); Object-Oriented UX with Sophia Prater, InfoQ interview (https://www.infoq.com/podcasts/object-oriented-ux-sophia-prater/); Prioritizing Prioritization for Product Designers, Sophia V. #### 105. Four UX Fails in OOUX
- **URL:** https://lexkonovalov.com/glossary/ooux-ux-fails.html
- **Category:** UX & Product Architecture (Secondary: Design Systems & Engineering)
- **Maturity:** Proprietary / Framework-Specific
- **Definition:** The four UX fails in Object-Oriented UX (OOUX) are masked, shape-shifting, broken, and isolated objects. Sophia Prater uses these patterns to diagnose why people may struggle to recognize objects, understand them across views, find their actions, or reach related records.
- **Purpose:** The four UX fails in Object-Oriented UX (OOUX) are masked, shape-shifting, broken, and isolated objects. Sophia Prater uses these patterns to diagnose why people may struggle to recognize objects, understand them across views, find their actions, or reach related records.

#### 107. ORCA Relationship Requirements

Sophia Prater uses MCSFD as a checklist for five decisions: mechanics, cardinality, sorting, filtering, and dependency. Teams use it to turn a relationship they discovered into rules they can design and test.
- **Purpose:** ORCA relationship requirements describe how a connection between objects works in a product. #### 108. Junction Object
- **URL:** https://lexkonovalov.com/glossary/junction-object.html
- **Category:** UX & Product Architecture (Secondary: Design Systems & Engineering)
- **Maturity:** Proprietary / Framework-Specific
- **Definition:** A junction object represents a relationship as an object in its own right. It is useful when the connection itself carries information that matters to users. In Object-Oriented UX (OOUX), it gives that information a clear place in the model and helps teams decide where people should see or change it.
- **Purpose:** A junction object represents a relationship as an object in its own right. It is useful when the connection itself carries information that matters to users. In Object-Oriented UX (OOUX), it gives that information a clear place in the model and helps teams decide where people should see or change it.
- **Key Concepts:** Example of a junction object, When is a junction object useful?, How does it show up in the interface?
- **How It Works:** A junction object represents a relationship as an object in its own right. It is useful when the connection itself carries information that matters to users. In Object-Oriented UX (OOUX), it gives that information a clear place in the model and helps teams decide where people should see or change it.
- **Related Terms:** Object Mapping, Cardinality (UX Architecture), Nested Object Matrix, ORCA Relationship Requirements
- **SEO Title:** Junction Objects in OOUX | Product Design Glossary

#### 109. User Retention

- **Category:** Product Strategy & Growth
- **Maturity:** Established
- **Definition:** User retention measures how many people in a starting group return to use a product over time. A retention rate uses a defined group, a return behavior, and a time window. For a product used by teams, the same approach can measure retention at the account level.
- **Purpose:** User retention measures how many people in a starting group return to use a product over time. A retention rate uses a defined group, a return behavior, and a time window. For a product used by teams, the same approach can measure retention at the account level.

#### 110. Product-Qualified Lead (PQL)
- **URL:** https://lexkonovalov.com/glossary/product-qualified-lead-pql.html
- **Category:** Product Strategy & Growth
- **Maturity:** Established
- **Definition:** A product-qualified lead (PQL) is a prospective buyer whose product use provides evidence that they may be ready to purchase. Teams combine usage with customer fit and intent to decide whether to offer help, route the lead to sales, or keep the experience self-service.
- **Purpose:** A product-qualified lead (PQL) is a prospective buyer whose product use provides evidence that they may be ready to purchase. Teams combine usage with customer fit and intent to decide whether to offer help, route the lead to sales, or keep the experience self-service.

- **How It Works:** A product-qualified lead (PQL) is a prospective buyer whose product use provides evidence that they may be ready to purchase. Teams combine usage with customer fit and intent to decide whether to offer help, route the lead to sales, or keep the experience self-service.
- **Related Terms:** Product-Led Growth (PLG), Activation Metric, Lead Capture, Product Telemetry & Analytics
- **SEO Title:** Product-Qualified Lead (PQL) | Product Design Glossary

#### 111. European Accessibility Act (EAA)
- **URL:** https://lexkonovalov.com/glossary/european-accessibility-act.html
- **Category:** Design Systems & Engineering (Secondary: UX & Product Architecture)
- **Maturity:** Established
- **Definition:** The European Accessibility Act (EAA) is an EU directive that sets accessibility requirements for certain products and services sold or provided in the EU. It covers consumer e-commerce, consumer banking, e-books, and specified digital aspects of passenger transport, among other services. The directive sets June 28, 2025, as the start date for applying national measures, with transition provisions for some cases.
- **Purpose:** The European Accessibility Act (EAA) is an EU directive that sets accessibility requirements for certain products and services sold or provided in the EU. It covers consumer e-commerce, consumer banking, e-books, and specified digital aspects of passenger transport, among other services. The directive sets June 28, 2025, as the start date for applying national measures, with transition provisions for some cases.
- **Key Concepts:** Which websites and apps does the EAA cover?, What should a product team check in checkout?, How does the EAA relate to WCAG and EN 301 549?
- **How It Works:** The European Accessibility Act (EAA) is an EU directive that sets accessibility requirements for certain products and services sold or provided in the EU. It covers consumer e-commerce, consumer banking, e-books, and specified digital aspects of passenger transport, among other services. The directive sets June 28, 2025, as the start date for applying national measures, with transition provisions for some cases.
- **Related Terms:** Accessibility and WCAG, EN 301 549, Web Accessibility Audit, ADA Web Accessibility
- **SEO Title:** European Accessibility Act (EAA) for Digital Products
- **Sources:** Directive (EU) 2019/882, EUR-Lex (https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2019/882/oj?uri=CELEX%3A32019L0882); Accessibility Requirements for Products and Services, Your Europe (https://europa.eu/youreurope/business/selling-in-eu/selling-goods-services/accessibility/indexamp_en.htm); European Accessibility Act, Council of the European Union (https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/policies/accessibility-goods-services/)

#### 112. EN 301 549
- **URL:** https://lexkonovalov.com/glossary/en-301-549.html
- **Category:** Design Systems & Engineering (Secondary: UX & Product Architecture)
- **Maturity:** Established
- **Definition:** EN 301 549 is a European technical standard for accessibility in information and communication technology (ICT). It covers web content, non-web documents, software, hardware, and services. Its web requirements draw on WCAG, and its other clauses address accessibility needs specific to different products and services.
- **Purpose:** EN 301 549 is a European technical standard for accessibility in information and communication technology (ICT). #### 113. ADA Web Accessibility
- **URL:** https://lexkonovalov.com/glossary/ada-web-accessibility.html

- **Maturity:** Established
- **Definition:** ADA web accessibility refers to providing people with disabilities access to online services under the Americans with Disabilities Act. Title II applies to U.S. state and local government entities. Title III applies to businesses and nonprofits that qualify as places of public accommodation.

#### 114. Section 508
- **URL:** https://lexkonovalov.com/glossary/section-508.html
- **Category:** Design Systems & Engineering (Secondary: UX & Product Architecture)
- **Maturity:** Established
- **Definition:** Section 508 of the Rehabilitation Act requires U.S. federal agencies to make covered information and communication technology (ICT) accessible when they develop, procure, maintain, or use it. The Revised Section 508 Standards cover areas such as websites, electronic documents, software, hardware, and support documentation.
- **Purpose:** Section 508 of the Rehabilitation Act requires U.S. federal agencies to make covered information and communication technology (ICT) accessible when they develop, procure, maintain, or use it. The Revised Section 508 Standards cover areas such as websites, electronic documents, software, hardware, and support documentation.

- **How It Works:** Section 508 of the Rehabilitation Act requires U.S. federal agencies to make covered information and communication technology (ICT) accessible when they develop, procure, maintain, or use it. The Revised Section 508 Standards cover areas such as websites, electronic documents, software, hardware, and support documentation.

#### 115. Web Accessibility Audit

- **Definition:** A web accessibility audit is a documented evaluation of a website or web app against a defined accessibility standard and scope. It identifies barriers, records how they were found, and gives teams evidence they can use to prioritize fixes and verify changes.

#### 120. Object Representation
- **URL:** https://lexkonovalov.com/glossary/object-representation-ooux.html
- **Category:** UX & Product Architecture
- **Maturity:** Proprietary / Framework-Specific
- **Definition:** Object representation in OOUX is the way an interface makes an object recognizable and usable through its information, visual treatment, relationships, and actions. Examples include a booking row, a traveler card, and a detailed trip view.
- **Purpose:** Object representation in OOUX is the way an interface makes an object recognizable and usable through its information, visual treatment, relationships, and actions. Examples include a booking row, a traveler card, and a detailed trip view.
- **Key Concepts:** Start with the user's question, Example: representing Booking B-52, Keep meaningful differences visible, Check behavior and accessibility
- **How It Works:** Object representation in OOUX is the way an interface makes an object recognizable and usable through its information, visual treatment, relationships, and actions. Examples include a booking row, a traveler card, and a detailed trip view.
- **Related Terms:** Object Mapping, Shapeshifter Matrix, Attribute Prioritization, CTA Prioritization
- **SEO Title:** Object Representation in OOUX: From Models to Interface

#### 121. Object-Oriented User Stories
- **URL:** https://lexkonovalov.com/glossary/object-oriented-user-stories.html
- **Category:** UX & Product Architecture
- **Maturity:** Proprietary / Framework-Specific
- **Definition:** Object-oriented user stories describe what a particular actor needs to do to an object, why the action matters, and when it is appropriate. In ORCA, teams develop them from CTA Matrix entries during the Requirements round.
- **Purpose:** Object-oriented user stories describe what a particular actor needs to do to an object, why the action matters, and when it is appropriate. In ORCA, teams develop them from CTA Matrix entries during the Requirements round.

- **How It Works:** Object-oriented user stories describe what a particular actor needs to do to an object, why the action matters, and when it is appropriate. In ORCA, teams develop them from CTA Matrix entries during the Requirements round.

#### 123. ORCA Sprint

- **Definition:** An ORCA Sprint is a focused, collaborative workshop format that applies OOUX's Objects, Relationships, Calls-to-Action, and Attributes to a defined design problem. OOUX describes a one-week format involving designers, developers, domain experts, business stakeholders, and content practitioners.
- **Purpose:** An ORCA Sprint is a focused, collaborative workshop format that applies OOUX's Objects, Relationships, Calls-to-Action, and Attributes to a defined design problem. OOUX describes a one-week format involving designers, developers, domain experts, business stakeholders, and content practitioners.

OOUX describes a one-week format involving designers, developers, domain experts, business stakeholders, and content practitioners.

#### 128. Tree Systems in OOUX
- **URL:** https://lexkonovalov.com/glossary/tree-systems-ooux.html
- **Category:** UX & Product Architecture
- **Maturity:** Proprietary / Framework-Specific
- **Definition:** A Tree System in OOUX is a pattern of related object types that move from a general concept toward more specific, contextual forms. It includes a root, a more specific “fruit” object, and sometimes intermediate “branch” objects.
- **Purpose:** A Tree System in OOUX is a pattern of related object types that move from a general concept toward more specific, contextual forms. It includes a root, a more specific “fruit” object, and sometimes intermediate “branch” objects.
- **Key Concepts:** Example: a course and its scheduled sessions, Where should information belong?, Tree Systems, hierarchy, and inheritance, How to check the model
- **How It Works:** A Tree System in OOUX is a pattern of related object types that move from a general concept toward more specific, contextual forms. It includes a root, a more specific “fruit” object, and sometimes intermediate “branch” objects.
- **Related Terms:** Junction Object, Object Inheritance in OOUX, Object Attributes in OOUX, Conceptual Schema
- **SEO Title:** Tree Systems in OOUX: Roots, Branches, and Specific Objects

#### 141. Theming
- **URL:** https://lexkonovalov.com/glossary/design-system-theming.html
- **Category:** Design Systems & Engineering
- **Maturity:** Established
- **Definition:** Theming is the practice of applying a coordinated set of design values to a shared interface. In a design system, a theme can change colors, typography, or other supported decisions while components retain a consistent purpose and API.
- **Purpose:** Theming is the practice of applying a coordinated set of design values to a shared interface. In a design system, a theme can change colors, typography, or other supported decisions while components retain a consistent purpose and API.
- **Key Concepts:** How does theming work with design tokens?, Theme vs. mode vs. component variant, Example: two brands with light and dark appearances, What should you test across themes?
- **How It Works:** Theming is the practice of applying a coordinated set of design values to a shared interface. In a design system, a theme can change colors, typography, or other supported decisions while components retain a consistent purpose and API.

- **Maturity:** Established

#### 149. Touch Target Size
- **URL:** https://lexkonovalov.com/glossary/touch-target-size.html
- **Category:** Design Systems & Engineering (Secondary: UX & Product Architecture)
- **Maturity:** Established
- **Definition:** Touch target size is the width and height of the area that responds when someone taps or clicks a control. WCAG 2.2 applies its target-size criteria to pointer inputs, including touch and mouse. Measure the interactive area of the control, including any padding that can receive input.
- **Purpose:** Touch target size is the width and height of the area that responds when someone taps or clicks a control. WCAG 2.2 applies its target-size criteria to pointer inputs, including touch and mouse. Measure the interactive area of the control, including any padding that can receive input.
- **Key Concepts:** What target size does WCAG require?, Example: Edit and delete buttons in a table
- **How It Works:** Touch target size is the width and height of the area that responds when someone taps or clicks a control. WCAG 2.2 applies its target-size criteria to pointer inputs, including touch and mouse. Measure the interactive area of the control, including any padding that can receive input.

#### 150. WCAG Color Contrast

- **Category:** Design Systems & Engineering (Secondary: UX & Product Architecture)
- **Maturity:** Established
- **Definition:** WCAG color contrast measures the difference in relative luminance between two colors. WCAG uses contrast ratios to set minimums for text and for visual information people need to identify interface controls, states, and graphics.

#### 151. Zoom, Text Resize & Reflow
- **URL:** https://lexkonovalov.com/glossary/zoom-text-resize-reflow.html
- **Category:** Design Systems & Engineering (Secondary: UX & Product Architecture)
- **Maturity:** Established
- **Definition:** Page zoom enlarges the rendered page. Text resizing lets people make the text larger. Reflow is how content rearranges to fit the available space so people can read and interact without scrolling in two directions.
- **Purpose:** Page zoom enlarges the rendered page. Text resizing lets people make the text larger. Reflow is how content rearranges to fit the available space so people can read and interact without scrolling in two directions.
- **Key Concepts:** What are the two WCAG checks?, Example: A booking form with a fare table, How do you test reflow?
- **How It Works:** Page zoom enlarges the rendered page. Text resizing lets people make the text larger. Reflow is how content rearranges to fit the available space so people can read and interact without scrolling in two directions.
- **Related Terms:** Accessibility and WCAG, Accessible Forms, Keyboard Accessibility & Focus Management, Touch Target Size, Fluid Typography & Spacing System, Web Accessibility Audit
- **SEO Title:** WCAG Zoom, Text Resize & Reflow: 200% and 320 CSS px

#### 161. Prompt Injection
- **URL:** https://lexkonovalov.com/glossary/prompt-injection.html
- **Category:** AI & Agentic Systems
- **Maturity:** Established
- **Definition:** Prompt injection is an attack that puts instructions into content an AI system processes, attempting to redirect its behavior beyond the intended task. The instructions may come from a direct user input or from an external source such as a document or web page.
- **Purpose:** Prompt injection is an attack that puts instructions into content an AI system processes, attempting to redirect its behavior beyond the intended task. The instructions may come from a direct user input or from an external source such as a document or web page.
- **Key Concepts:** Direct vs. indirect prompt injection, Example: a supplier document in an operations tool, What belongs in the product design?, Why are system prompts insufficient?
- **How It Works:** Prompt injection is an attack that puts instructions into content an AI system processes, attempting to redirect its behavior beyond the intended task. The instructions may come from a direct user input or from an external source such as a document or web page.
- **Related Terms:** System Prompts and Guardrails, Tool Calling, Agentic UX, Human-in-the-Loop
- **SEO Title:** Prompt Injection and AI Workflows | Product Design Glossary
- **Sources:** Prompt Injection, OWASP Gen AI Security Project (https://genai.owasp.org/llmrisk/llm01-prompt-injection/); Prompt Shields, Microsoft Learn (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-services/content-safety/concepts/jailbreak-detection)

- **Definition:** Structured outputs are model responses constrained to a specified format or schema. They let an application request defined fields and types, such as a reservation identifier and a status, instead of interpreting an unrestricted text answer.
- **Purpose:** Structured outputs are model responses constrained to a specified format or schema. They let an application request defined fields and types, such as a reservation identifier and a status, instead of interpreting an unrestricted text answer.

#### 164. Trust Calibration in AI
- **URL:** https://lexkonovalov.com/glossary/trust-calibration-ai.html
- **Category:** AI & Agentic Systems
- **Maturity:** Established
- **Definition:** Trust calibration in AI is the alignment between a person's expectations of a system and its actual capabilities and limitations. The design goal is appropriate reliance: helping people use valid outputs and recognize when verification, correction, or another approach is needed.
- **Purpose:** Trust calibration in AI is the alignment between a person's expectations of a system and its actual capabilities and limitations. The design goal is appropriate reliance: helping people use valid outputs and recognize when verification, correction, or another approach is needed.

#### 165. AI Unit Economics
- **URL:** https://lexkonovalov.com/glossary/ai-unit-economics.html
- **Category:** Product Strategy & Growth
- **Maturity:** Established
- **Definition:** AI unit economics is the analysis of revenue and costs for a defined unit of an AI product, such as a customer account or a completed task. Task-level analysis includes model use, tools, retries, failed runs, and any human work within the stated cost boundary.
- **Purpose:** AI unit economics is the analysis of revenue and costs for a defined unit of an AI product, such as a customer account or a completed task. Task-level analysis includes model use, tools, retries, failed runs, and any human work within the stated cost boundary.

#### 167. Contribution Margin
- **URL:** https://lexkonovalov.com/glossary/contribution-margin.html
- **Category:** Product Strategy & Growth
- **Maturity:** Established
- **Definition:** Contribution margin is revenue minus variable costs. It shows how much remains to cover fixed costs and, once those costs are covered, contribute to operating profit. It can be expressed as a total amount, an amount per unit, or a percentage of revenue.
- **Purpose:** Contribution margin is revenue minus variable costs. It shows how much remains to cover fixed costs and, once those costs are covered, contribute to operating profit. It can be expressed as a total amount, an amount per unit, or a percentage of revenue.
- **Key Concepts:** What are the contribution margin formulas?, A SaaS contribution margin example, Why can contribution margin differ from gross margin?, How does contribution margin inform product decisions?, What should designers avoid?
- **How It Works:** Contribution margin is revenue minus variable costs. It shows how much remains to cover fixed costs and, once those costs are covered, contribute to operating profit. It can be expressed as a total amount, an amount per unit, or a percentage of revenue.
- **Related Terms:** Gross Margin, Unit Economics, Cost to Serve, Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC)
- **SEO Title:** Contribution Margin: Formula, Example, and Gross Margin
- **Sources:** OpenStax: Contribution margin per unit, ratio, and total (https://openstax.org/books/principles-managerial-accounting/pages/3-1-explain-contribution-margin-and-calculate-contribution-margin-per-unit-contribution-margin-ratio-and-total-contribution-margin); Stripe: Variable costs and ecommerce profitability (https://stripe.com/resources/more/variable-costs-and-ecommerce-profitability); SEC: Beginners' Guide to Financial Statements (https://www.sec.gov/investor/pubs/begfinstmtguide.htm)

#### 169. Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC)
- **URL:** https://lexkonovalov.com/glossary/customer-acquisition-cost-cac.html
- **Category:** Product Strategy & Growth
- **Maturity:** Established
- **Definition:** Customer acquisition cost (CAC) is the average cost of acquiring a new customer. For the SaaS model used here, it equals acquisition-related sales and marketing costs divided by the number of new paying customer accounts acquired.
- **Purpose:** Customer acquisition cost (CAC) is the average cost of acquiring a new customer. For the SaaS model used here, it equals acquisition-related sales and marketing costs divided by the number of new paying customer accounts acquired.
- **Key Concepts:** How do you calculate CAC?, A CAC calculation example, CAC vs. CPA and blended vs. paid CAC, What makes a CAC estimate misleading?, How can product designers use CAC?
- **How It Works:** Customer acquisition cost (CAC) is the average cost of acquiring a new customer. For the SaaS model used here, it equals acquisition-related sales and marketing costs divided by the number of new paying customer accounts acquired.
- **Related Terms:** Unit Economics, LTV to CAC Ratio, CAC Payback Period, Conversion Rate Optimization (CRO), Product-Led Growth (PLG)
- **SEO Title:** Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC): Formula and Example
- **Sources:** Stripe: CAC in SaaS (https://stripe.com/resources/more/cac-in-saas); David Skok: SaaS Metrics 2.0 — Detailed Definitions (https://www.forentrepreneurs.com/saas-metrics-2-definitions/)

#### 171. Gross Margin
- **URL:** https://lexkonovalov.com/glossary/gross-margin.html
- **Category:** Product Strategy & Growth
- **Maturity:** Established
- **Definition:** Gross margin is the percentage of revenue remaining after subtracting cost of goods sold or cost of revenue. Gross profit is the corresponding dollar amount. Both measures describe delivery economics before other expenses are deducted.
- **Purpose:** Gross margin is the percentage of revenue remaining after subtracting cost of goods sold or cost of revenue. Gross profit is the corresponding dollar amount. Both measures describe delivery economics before other expenses are deducted.
- **Key Concepts:** How do you calculate gross margin?, A SaaS gross margin example, What belongs in SaaS cost of revenue?, Gross margin vs. contribution margin, How can product designers use gross margin?
- **How It Works:** Gross margin is the percentage of revenue remaining after subtracting cost of goods sold or cost of revenue. Gross profit is the corresponding dollar amount. Both measures describe delivery economics before other expenses are deducted.
- **Related Terms:** Unit Economics, Contribution Margin, Cost to Serve, Customer Lifetime Value (LTV)
- **SEO Title:** Gross Margin: Formula, SaaS Example, and Cost Boundaries
- **Sources:** SEC: Beginners' Guide to Financial Statements (https://www.sec.gov/investor/pubs/begfinstmtguide.htm); Stripe: SaaS gross margin explained (https://stripe.com/resources/more/saas-gross-margin-explained-what-it-is-and-why-it-is-important); OpenStax: Contribution margin and cost behavior (https://openstax.org/books/principles-managerial-accounting/pages/3-1-explain-contribution-margin-and-calculate-contribution-margin-per-unit-contribution-margin-ratio-and-total-contribution-margin)

#### 172. Net Revenue Retention (NRR)
- **URL:** https://lexkonovalov.com/glossary/net-revenue-retention-nrr.html
- **Category:** Product Strategy & Growth
- **Maturity:** Established
- **Definition:** Net revenue retention (NRR), also called net dollar retention (NDR), measures recurring revenue retained from an existing customer group over a defined period, including expansion and losses from contraction and churn. It excludes revenue from new customers.
- **Purpose:** Net revenue retention (NRR), also called net dollar retention (NDR), measures recurring revenue retained from an existing customer group over a defined period, including expansion and losses from contraction and churn. It excludes revenue from new customers.
- **Key Concepts:** What is the NRR formula?, An NRR calculation example, NRR vs. GRR vs. customer retention, How should you handle reactivation?, What can product designers learn from NRR?
- **How It Works:** Net revenue retention (NRR), also called net dollar retention (NDR), measures recurring revenue retained from an existing customer group over a defined period, including expansion and losses from contraction and churn. It excludes revenue from new customers.
- **Related Terms:** User Retention, Customer Lifetime Value (LTV), Gross Margin, Product-Led Growth (PLG)
- **SEO Title:** Net Revenue Retention (NRR): Formula, Example, and GRR
- **Sources:** ChartMogul: Net MRR Retention report (https://help.chartmogul.com/article/143-chart-net-mrr-retention); ChartMogul: Gross MRR Retention report (https://help.chartmogul.com/article/142-chart-gross-mrr-retention); ChartMogul: Cohort Net MRR Retention (https://help.chartmogul.com/article/160-cohort-net-mrr-retention)

#### 173. Outcome-Based Pricing
- **URL:** https://lexkonovalov.com/glossary/outcome-based-pricing.html
- **Category:** Product Strategy & Growth
- **Maturity:** Established
- **Definition:** Outcome-based pricing ties a charge to a defined result rather than only to access, time, or activity. In an AI product, the result might be a resolved support case or an accepted document extraction, with explicit rules for what counts and when it becomes billable.
- **Purpose:** Outcome-based pricing ties a charge to a defined result rather than only to access, time, or activity. In an AI product, the result might be a resolved support case or an accepted document extraction, with explicit rules for what counts and when it becomes billable.

- **How It Works:** Outcome-based pricing ties a charge to a defined result rather than only to access, time, or activity. In an AI product, the result might be a resolved support case or an accepted document extraction, with explicit rules for what counts and when it becomes billable.
- **Related Terms:** Usage-Based Pricing, Pricing Metric, AI Unit Economics, Cost to Serve
- **SEO Title:** Outcome-Based Pricing: Definition, AI Examples, and UX

#### 174. Pricing Metric

- **Definition:** A pricing metric is the unit a product uses to calculate what a customer pays, such as a licensed user, an API request, or a verified result. Choosing it determines what is counted as customers adopt the product and their needs change.

#### 175. Unit Economics

#### 176. Usage-Based Pricing
- **URL:** https://lexkonovalov.com/glossary/usage-based-pricing.html

- **Maturity:** Established
- **Definition:** Usage-based pricing charges customers according to a measured amount of product or service consumption, such as API requests, storage, or processed documents. It can be combined with a fixed subscription, included allowance, or prepaid credits.
- **Purpose:** Usage-based pricing charges customers according to a measured amount of product or service consumption, such as API requests, storage, or processed documents. It can be combined with a fixed subscription, included allowance, or prepaid credits.

- **How It Works:** Usage-based pricing charges customers according to a measured amount of product or service consumption, such as API requests, storage, or processed documents. It can be combined with a fixed subscription, included allowance, or prepaid credits.
